newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka expands search for missing military plane.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka expands search for missing military plane.

text.p: Sri Lankan air force planes and navy patrols have stepped up a search for a transport plane believed to have crashed at sea off northern Jaffna peninsula on Monday with four people aboard, an air force official said.
"We have not found anything yet and have expanded our search," he said.
The Y-12 twin-engined turbo-prop aircraft was on a maritime surveillance mission to check a suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) vessel when it lost radio contact, he said.
"The pilot gave a call around 5.15 a.m. (2315 GMT) saying he had seen a ship and was going down to identify her and that he will call after 10 minutes," the air force official said.
"When he did not call we tried to raise him. There was no response," he told Reuters. "We then started a search on the last known location."
The Y-12 had taken off about 4.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) from the Palaly airbase, in the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo, military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said.
"The aircraft lost radio contact about 75 miles (120 km) east of Palaly," Jayatunga told Reuters.
There were three air force officers and a navy petty officer on board, military officials said.
The vessel the pilot had gone to check was a merchant ship, they said.
The Y-12 is a transport aircraft but is often used in surveillance operations to look for rebel arms ships off the northern and eastern coasts.

The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, have shot down several air force planes using anti-aircraft missiles and guns since April 1995.
The government has said more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
